subject.title: Feature Request: Gateway lifecycle hooks (onSubagentComplete, onToolCallThreshold, onTurnComplete)

question: Which lifecycle hook contract should OpenClaw expose for subagent completion, turn completion, and tool-call thresholds: extend workspace/internal hooks, typed plugin hooks, or split those surfaces by sensitivity?
rationale: The request crosses API naming, payload data exposure, ordering, mid-turn execution, hook config, and plugin/workspace security boundaries, and current open PRs only cover parts of that decision.

options.title: Design one combined contract
options.body: Define the event names, payloads, and security rules once, then land a focused implementation with docs and tests across internal/workspace and typed plugin surfaces as appropriate.

options.title: Keep runtime control in plugin hooks
options.body: Expose sensitive or mid-turn lifecycle behavior only through typed plugin hooks and keep workspace/internal hooks for coarse operator automation.

options.title: Stage observation before thresholds
options.body: Land only observation-style completion events first, then decide threshold/mid-turn behavior separately after payload and injection semantics are settled.

recommendation.title: Design one combined contract
recommendation.body: Define the event names, payloads, and security rules once, then land a focused implementation with docs and tests across internal/workspace and typed plugin surfaces as appropriate.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest current history signal for internal hooks and published hook docs points to steipete, while plugin/subagent contributors should be included in the design review.
